summary: Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, later serving as professor at UC Santa Barbara and Rabindranath Tagore Professor Emeritus at Indiana University Bloomington.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 until 1950.
Gerd J. R. Mevissen specializes in Indology and archaeology/history. His career includes posts at the Free University of Berlin, where he was attested as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter.

Gereon Kopf focuses on philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University and under Yasuo Yuasa, holding posts at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong, alongside research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan universities.

Gergely Hidas works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Csaba Töttössy, and Ferenc Ruzsa, later holding posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the British Museum.
Gerhard Meiser was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Albertus-Magnus-Gymnasium Regensburg and the universities of Munich, Belgrade, Sarajevo, Regensburg, and Freiburg.

Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Innsbruck and the Sorbonne under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan, subsequently holding positions at Utrecht University and the University of Vienna.

Gerhard Wolf is a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg University from circa 1974 to 1989 and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, Trier University, and the Max Planck Society.
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg from circa 1961 to 1965. He held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from circa 1977 to 2002.
Gernot Rotter studied at the University of Bonn under Annemarie Schimmel and at the University of Tübingen. He held a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1984 to 1998.
Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld specialized in Indology. He studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he also worked, before holding a chair at the University of Regensburg.

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Khensur Ngawang Legden, later holding posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Virginia.

Geshe Jampa Tegchok worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery and held posts as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery and resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha.
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Gyume Tantric College and Sera Monastery.

Geshe Lhakdor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery, later serving at Tibet House and as Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Geshe Lhundup Sopa worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries under Geshe Lhundrup Tabkhe, Geshe Ngawang Rigsal, Geshe Ngawang Gendun, and Lhundrub Tsöndrü, later serving as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College.
Geshe Losang Chödar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Leiden University, Drepung Monastery, and Drepung Gomang Dratsang, and served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.
